subject: english-language-arts
instructions: Read the supplied text or source closely, then write an original analysis or composition.
Cite relevant evidence and revise for meaning, organization, and language before submitting.

learnerTasks.prompt: Explain author purpose and point of view in your own words and give or identify a valid example.
Use a diagram, model, quotation, data display, map, demonstration, or worked process to show understanding of rhetorical appeals.
Apply visual and audio framing in a new realistic situation. Show the process or cite evidence.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, unsafe choice, or design flaw involving algorithmic attention; correct it and explain why.
Connect author purpose and point of view with fact opinion and inference. Explain how the ideas support, constrain, contrast with, or build on one another.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit project: Analyze a message across two media and redesign it for accuracy, transparency, and audience.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy or quality, and one next question.

learnerSuccessCriteria: Provide evidence that meets the stated accuracy or fidelity criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated evidence and reasoning criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated application or performance criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated checking and revision criterion.
accommodations: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed.

provenance.unitObjective: How can the learner demonstrate the goals of Rhetoric, Media, and Information Ecosystems?
